appraisal_events.evidence: Through a third marriage, following the duc de Duras, she becomes princesse de Guermantes and holds "une grande situation" in the faubourg Saint-Germain that would have astonished Combray.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator reports a real, formal rise in rank: through successive marriages, the former Mme Verdurin has attained the highest title and standing in aristocratic society.

appraisal_events.evidence: Combray acquaintances say "la duchesse de Duras" while sneering, as if it were a stage role, and society concludes "que c'était un faux Guermantes, un escroc"; the narrator notes the title itself "faisait plutôt mauvais effet."
appraisal_events.explanation: Despite her formal ascent, the passage shows her new title greeted with mockery and suspicion of illegitimacy, discrediting the very elevation just described.

status_effects.explanation: She now formally holds the title and social position of princesse de Guermantes, a witnessed rise to the top of the faubourg Saint-Germain hierarchy.
She is locally discredited as an impostor or fraud by the collective social voice, which mocks her borrowed grandeur and treats her new name as illegitimate.

ambiguities: The bare surface form "princesse de Guermantes" in this passage is explicitly resolved within the text itself to Mme Verdurin (the narrator clarifies that the original princesse is dead), so it is not treated here as an unresolved ambiguity.
